keep_playing_why: B has a verb with real trade-offs: charging your lance under a storm cell makes the next hit stronger but forbids striking while you are under it, the AI gets zapped too, and the gap gauge, crest height and ring timing all feed the same strike. Each captain forces a different line (Barnacle rams, Kite flies), and by minute five I played differently than in minute one. A has one lovely idea (the tide dial as terrain, boat and boss weapon) but the whole story took 5 minutes and the guided prompts left one right answer at each step.
better_made_why: B has chunkier juice (hit stops, stings, captain barks, VS cards, medals, a ladder and a Dock), per-stage music and a consistent look, though its pause menu is visibly broken (two stretched cream panels) and onboarding text is easy to miss. A looks like a finished little film with a nice boss and a good lantern/tide fantasy, but showed blank or black frames after several walks, a visible edge on the sea at the finale and an empty world after the credits with the 5 lost things unreachable.
furthest_A: Finished the whole story in about 5 min: harbour, Well Islet, Tam's boat, Sand Bar, Shellflats wreck lens, the Needles boat run, the 3-hit Undertow boss, lit the lighthouse and got the credits card (5 min, 73 m of sea moved, 3 knocks, 0 of 5 lost things found). Played on in free roam afterwards.
furthest_B: Squall Cup: beat Pip Tiller twice (scores 2,000 and 1,800, medals Sky Knight and Thunderstruck, won his yacht The Bathtub and equipped it). Reached Bosun Barnacle (captain 2) but lost to him four times (best state 2 footing vs his 5, then 1 v 2). Also lost to Kite Kowalski in Endless Squall after trading a hit (streak 0, best score 100).
